results.title: Engineers sent robotic “sensor fish” through a Columbia River dam, then subjected 5,767 young salmon to the same pressure drop — revealing that turbine blades are rarely what kill them; their swim bladders expand so violently that organs rupture and gas bubbles lodge in their gills
results.description: The real killer inside hydroelectric dams isn't the spinning blades—it's physics: the sudden pressure drop forces fish swim bladders to rupture and sends fatal gas bubbles into their gills. The post Engineers sent robotic “sensor fish” through a Columbia River dam, then subjected 5,767 young salmon to the same pressure drop — revealing that turbine blades are rarely what kill them; their swim bladders expand so violently that organs rupture and gas bubbles lodge in their gills appeared first on Space Daily .
